aliases: Lijiang Snow White Tea (Earth Tea, Taibai Tea)

brewing.notes: A common starting point for herbal infusions: boiling water, about five minutes.

description:
A white lichen from Yulong County near Lijiang, drunk as an infusion though it is not tea at all. It grows wild in the moss belt above 4000 metres and cannot be cultivated.

Brew it as you would other herbal infusions. If the plant is new to you, check that it is safe for you first, especially when pregnant or on medication.
history: Local accounts say it was already a tribute item of the Mu chieftains in the Ming dynasty. The Qing materia medica Bencao Gangmu Shiyi notes that it is not really tea and that locals gathered and fired it to drink in place of tea. Several Lijiang companies now box it for visitors.
processing: Dried plant material, as with most herbal infusions.
harvest_season: Depends on the plant and the place.
appearance_dry: Very light, hollow, snow-white strands 30 to 70 mm long and 1 to 3 mm thick.
appearance_liquor: Depends on the plant; usually pale to amber.
taste_profile: Bitter at first, turning sweet when chewed or sipped.
vintage_note: Herbal infusions are not sold by vintage: buy recent stock and use it within a year or so.
